sample.title: The Most Profitable Subway on Earth
sample.description:
Hong Kong’s Mass Transit Railway is the most profitable transit system in the world. While subways tend to lose money everywhere else, the MTR funds its system through a real estate engine known as “land-value capture.” By directly integrating malls, offices and apartments into stations, the railway has created a self-funding loop that pays billions of dollars back to the government.

Now, the MTR is taking on a massive challenge: funding transport for the Northern Metropolis, a new tech hub aimed at better connecting Hong Kong with Mainland China. But as local real estate cools, construction costs soar and residents shift retail spending across the border to Shenzhen, the MTR is taking on record debt to fund the expansion. Will this ambitious project break the very rule that made Hong Kong’s transit a global marvel?

sample.description:
The U.S. is on track to lose its official measles-free elimination status, as cases have soared across the country. Health experts warn that this could be indicative of more problems to come. Vaccination rates for a variety of diseases – that have been largely pushed out of the U.S. – have been falling in recent years. Steeper declines could lead to millions of new cases in the coming years, according to scientific prediction models. Watch the video to learn about what this means for public health.

sample.title: Watch live: Dozens feared dead in Spain after two high-speed trains collide | BBC News
sample.description:
The death toll is continuing to rise after two trains collided south of Madrid in Spain. Watch live for updates on what we know so far.

More than 500 passengers were travelling on the trains involved, and the death toll "will almost certainly rise", according to the spokesperson for the regional government.

Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says he is "shocked by the serious train accident" and is in constant contact with the transport minister.

Rail operator Adif says the incident occurred between a Renfe train and another of the Iryo company, which covers the Madrid to Seville route.

A spokesperson for the Spanish emergency services tells AFP "all resources are currently being deployed" including "several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units".
